text:
Maya Patel: quick update — tried the coalescer change (queue_coalesce_ms=5) on canary; weird perf shape on mixed-short workloads where FlashAttention seems to lose efficiency.
Samir Gupta: can you paste the flame/profile? sounds like kernel switching may be thrashing.
Maya Patel: attaching the quick perf dump i grabbed from canary run:
```
Profile summary (canary-2026-03-12):
- workload: 60% short (seq<=32), 40% mid (seq 64-128)
- config: token_budget_target=2048 -> coalescer queue_coalesce_ms=5
- observed: end-to-end throughput -5%, p99 latency +18%
- kernel breakdown (tokens/s):
  FlashAttention (seq<=64): 95k tok/s
  FlashAttention (seq 65-128): 210k tok/s
  non-flash (fallback): 240k tok/s
- paged-KV hit-rate: 0.87, but page-reads spiking on short prefixes (tail)
```
Alex B.: interesting — raw kernel numbers show non-flash beating flash for mid seq, but flash is supposed to win on short. maybe the batching is coalescing incompatible seqs and losing vectorization.
Julia Park: we saw similar during last week's A/B where hybrid-kernel routing was too eager to pick flash when KV page misses caused stall. If the batch includes both hot-cached and cold-prefetch items, flash's memory pattern degrades.
Ken O'Leary: could also be token-budget math. With coalesce_ms=5 we packed more short requests into big logical batches and triggered paged-KV eviction or aggressive prefetch, so kernel becomes memory-bound.
Maya Patel: i tried toggling token_budget_target -> 1024 and observed improvement: throughput -1%, p99 +6% (better but not ideal). full numbers below.
```
A/B snapshots:
- token_budget_target=2048: throughput -5%, p99 +18%
- token_budget_target=1024: throughput -1%, p99 +6%
- token_budget_target=512: throughput +2%, p99 +12% (weird: throughput up but latency jitter high)
```
Samir Gupta: odd that 512 ups throughput but increases p99. that smells like queue starvation + microbursting. small token budgets let many tiny batches go through Flash paths with tiny kernels; overhead per-batch dominates p99.
Alex B.: exactly. propose we try kernel-aware batching: when predicted seq distribution skewed (high short fraction) bias token_budget_target upward for batches that are flash-eligible, and add a hard limit on mixed-seq coalesce (reject mixing seq<32 with seq>64 in same batch).
Julia Park: +1 for no-mix rule. also add a paged-KV backpressure metric into batch formation: if page-read-rate > X, prioritize non-flash kernels or split batches to avoid memory stalls.
Ken O'Leary: here's a config prototype I sketched — conservative defaults:
```yaml
batcher:
  token_budget_target: 1024
  queue_coalesce_ms: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 65536
  kernel_mix_policy:
    allow_mixed_seq: false
    short_seq_threshold: 32
    prefer_nonflash_if_page_reads_gt: 1000_per_min
paged_kv:
  backpressure_page_reads_threshold: 1000
  prefetch_limit: 4
```
Maya Patel: i pushed a canary with that policy; infra-bot will report canary status.
infra-bot: canary deploy started: canary-2026-03-12-ken-policy (10 hosts). watching p50/p95/p99 and page-read-rate.
(10m later)
infra-bot: canary metrics: throughput +1.8%, p99 -9%, page-read-rate -28% relative to previous canary.
Samir Gupta: nice. can you also capture kernel switch counts? we need to ensure we aren't just moving latency into scheduling.
Maya Patel: kernel-switch delta looks good: flash->nonflash falls by ~42% on mixed workload, total switches down 31%.
Alex B.: actionable items:
- (Maya) run 4-hour soak on canary with mixed load (we have test generator) and collect kernel-switch, page-read, batch-size distribution
- (Samir) add telemetry to batcher that emits "batch_seq_signature" (short|mid|mix) and chosen_kernel label for downstream joins
- (Julia) tune paged-KV prefetch_limit adaptive logic (start 4, ramp down when page_reads high)
- (Ken) prep rollback knob for kernel_mix_policy.allow_mixed_seq (default true)
Maya Patel: logging notes — keep payload minimal: just batch_id, batch_tokens, seq_stats, kernel_choice, page_reads at enqueue. don't log request bodies.
Ken O'Leary: i'll put PR up for the config and canary pipeline later today.
Julia Park: also add a tiny unit test for the "no-mix" batcher predicate (simulate seq set -> expect split).
Samir Gupta: thanks team — this feels like the right middle ground: prevent pathological mixing and make batching aware of KV pressure.
Maya Patel: will drop the soak results in this thread when done. :thumbsup:
Alex B.: great work. if soak is clean we can flip the policy for dedicated pools next week. :rocket:
